title: Gnomes Are Terrible at Taking Orders

pages.text:
*From the Dropout Club Handbook, Rule 12: Gnomes are terrible at taking orders.*

Bunt’s vest pockets were the size of small rooms, and he filled them with dignity. He walked across the Great Hall in slow, creaking steps, his barrel-boots thumping against the marble. Inside his left pocket, two fishmongers argued about the draft. Inside his right, a vice-principal demanded a chair. In the back, a choir section hummed a low, annoyed note.

"Gnome Relocation Services," Bunt announced softly, his voice like a boulder rolling under a rug. "Please remain seated. Or standing, if you prefer. Or hovering, though I suspect that is difficult for clay."

A gnome in a blue jacket popped his head out. "It is draughty!" he squeaked.

"I am sorry," Bunt said, reaching into his pocket with a hand the size of a dinner plate. "I will adjust the airflow." He did not know how to adjust the airflow. He simply pinched his nose and blew gently, which made the gnomes cough.

Marnie watched him go. It was absurd. It was also the only thing that was working.
pages.image: A large grey-green troll in a patched vest walks through a grand hall, his massive pockets bulging with tiny, angry garden gnomes in blue jackets and red hats; one gnome sticks its head out complaining.

pages.text:
The Potting Shed smelled of lavender and old wood. Lulu had built a nest of socks in the corner, hundreds of them, mismatched and soft, piled into a warm mountain for the gnomes to sleep in. The Principal-gnome sat on a flowerpot, his white beard stiff with dust. He looked furious, though he was only two feet tall.

"Tea," he squeaked. "Now. And where is my hat?"

Marnie blinked. The goose was sitting on the Principal’s head. He had not moved since they arrived. He looked as if the small, round head was a very good place to sit, and he was not going to leave.

Cassius-gnome stood apart from the group, his golden hair still perfect despite the chaos. He folded his arms. He refused to look at any of them. He simply stared at the wall, his painted smile fixed, his tiny body rigid with the effort of not screaming.

Lulu offered him a sock. He slapped it away.
pages.image: Inside a cozy potting shed, a tiny garden gnome with a white beard sits on a flowerpot looking angry, while Gerald with a purple ribbon sits calmly on his head; in the background, a tall, thin gnome in a blue blazer stands with arms folded in the corner.

pages.text:
Marnie had to get the notebook. She could feel the hex humming in the floorboards, a low vibration like a plucked string that hadn’t finished ringing. The Great Hall was empty now, except for the shimmer. The gold glitter wave had passed, leaving the floor bright and shiny and utterly, terrifyingly correct.

She walked backwards. Toby had taught her that. If you walked forward, your feet might accidentally cast a "Step" spell, and if it worked, you would be gnomed on the spot. Walking backwards, she was just a girl in red sneakers, clumsy and slow.

Gerald stood in the doorway. He did not honk. He did not steal a pencil. He just watched her with one orange eye, as if he knew exactly what she was doing and was waiting to see if she would be brave enough to finish it.

She reached the stage. The notebook was there, golden and gleaming.
pages.image: A girl with copper-red hair in buns and a green cloak walks backwards across a shiny, golden-tiled floor in an empty hall, reaching for a golden book on a stage; Gerald with a purple ribbon watches from the doorway.

pages.text:
The notebook’s last pages were scorched, the edges black and brittle. Marnie stood very still, though she knew breathing was safe. It was the magic that was the enemy. She turned the page, and a cloud of gold dust puffed out, drifting toward her face.

"Ah... ah... AH-CHOO!"

Bunt’s sneeze hit the dust like a hurricane. It blew the glitter clean off the page, settling it into his red-spotted handkerchief. The words were clear now. Cassius’s handwriting was tiny and precise, the way he cut his sandwiches.

*The Perfectly Perfect Spell requires a Balance Anchor: use the Founder's Hat, see Principal.*

And in the margin, in smaller, shakier letters: *Principal says replacement hat is fine?? It is NOT enchanted!*

Toby read it once. Then he read it again, his lips moving silently. His glasses fogged up. He looked at Marnie, and for the first time, his face was not dry or calm. It was scared.
pages.image: A close up of a golden notebook with scorched edges, open to a page with neat handwriting; a large troll’s hand holds a red-spotted handkerchief over the page, blowing away gold dust; a girl’s hands hold the book.

pages.text:
"What happened to the Principal's old hat?" Toby asked, his voice thin and quiet, like a pencil snapping in a silent library.

The silence that followed was heavy, the sort that sits on your chest when you know you have forgotten your homework and the teacher is about to turn around. Marnie stopped breathing for a second, then started again, her hands trembling in her lap like a deck of cards in a strong wind.

Lulu watched her, her head tilted to one side, the pink ribbon at the end of her braid swinging gently against her orange hoodie. She did not ask. She just waited, her eyes wide and patient, offering the kind of quiet support that felt safer than words.

Bunt, meanwhile, was staring at Gerald with the intense focus of someone watching a very dangerous insect. Gerald, completely unaware of the gravity of the situation, sneezed with a violent *honk* and snatched a polka-dot sock from Lulu’s pile, tucking it under his wing with the pride of a squirrel burying an acorn.

Marnie closed her eyes, counting to three in her head. She opened them.

"I turned it into a goose."
pages.image: Four children and Gerald stand in a circle in a dim room; the girl with red hair looks down at her hands with a shocked expression, while Gerald looks offended and a troll scratches his head in confusion.
